'''Gaoyong Zhang''' is an American mathematician. He is professor at the [[Courant Institute|Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] in New York City.  His main research interests are [[convex geometry]] and its connections with [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] and [[information theory]].

==Biography==
Gaoyong Zhang graduated from [[Temple University]] in Philadelphia with a PhD in 1995. His advisor was Eric Grinberg.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=40006 |title=Math Genealogy Gaoyong Zhang|accessdate= 12 September 2023}}</ref> Before he became a professor at the [[Courant Institute]] at [[NYU]], he was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study|Institute of Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/gaoyong-zhang|title= Past Member of the Institute of Advanced Study|date= 9 December 2019|accessdate=12 September 2023}}</ref>

Zhang became an Inaugural Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|website=Ams.org|accessdate=12 September 2023}}</ref> in 2012. He is a member of the editorial board at Advanced Nonlinear Studies (De Gruyter)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.degruyter.com/journal/key/ans/html#editorial|title=Advanced Nonlinear Studies – Editorial Board|accessdate=2023-09-12}}</ref> and at the [[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/journalsframework/procedit|title=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society – Editorial Board|accessdate=2023-09-12}}</ref>

==Work==
Gaoyong Zhang is known for his inverse of the Petty projection inequality,<ref>{{citation | last=Zhang | first=Gaoyong| title=Restricted chord projection and affine inequalities| journal=Geometriae Dedicata
| volume=39| date = 1991| issue=2| pages = 213–222| doi=10.1007/BF00182294| s2cid=123311639}}</ref> one of the few inequalities in convex geometry where simplices were proved to be extremals. He obtained a positive solution for the [[Busemann–Petty problem]] in <math>R^4</math>.<ref>{{citation|first=Gaoyong|last=Zhang|title=A positive solution to the Busemann-Petty problem in <math>\mathbb{R}^4</math> |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=149|year=1999|issue=2 |pages=535–543|doi=
10.2307/120974|jstor=120974 |s2cid=14663005 |doi-access=}}.</ref> He is known for his contributions (in collaboration with [[Erwin Lutwak]] and Deane Yang) to the L<sub>p</sub> Brunn Minkowski Theory and, in particular, his solution to the logarithmic Minkowski problem.<ref>{{citation
| last1=Böröczky | first1=Károly J.| last2=Lutwak | first2=Erwin| last3=Yang | first3=Deane| last4=Zhang | first4=Gaoyong| title=The logarithmic Minkowski problem
| journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]| volume=26| date=2013| issue=3| pages=831–852
| doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-2012-00741-3 | doi-access=free| url=http://real.mtak.hu/10063/1/carlos2.pdf}}.</ref>
